messages:
maria: quick follow-up on the prefetch + deferred-compaction RFC. noticed a couple of tail-latency cases when pinned tensors churn during traffic spikes. proposing a small set of safeguards (cooldown windows, amortized compaction, and a conservative fallback).

jonathan: can you sketch a concrete bad-path? curious how often this actually happens and whether it's tenant-specific or systemic. :thinking:

maria: example: tenant does rapid small requests, each alloc pins small KV-cache slices. we trigger compact-on-unpin which scans/folds slabs immediately. under high churn the compaction work competes with inference threads -> 100-300ms token latency spikes. saw it on two clusters last week.

lee: +1 to not compact synchronously on every unpin. idea: two-tier compaction: "soft compact" (cheap coalesce, O(1) per slab) that runs frequently, and "hard compact" (full reshuffle) that runs with a cooldown/backoff and only when memory pressure crosses a threshold.

rachel: we need telemetry before we change defaults. add counters for compaction_triggered:{soft,hard}, compaction_duration_ms, compaction_paused_reason, and a hist for post-compaction-latency. also trace correlation id so we can link to offending requests.

devx: API question: do we want these knobs exposed to Dedicated/Private customers? or keep hidden behind an "auto_safety" feature flag? if exposed, naming and units need to be clear.

maria: prefer opt-out for hosted (safe defaults) and full knobs for Dedicated/Private. proposed config snippet:

```yaml
memory.compaction:
  soft.enabled: true
  soft.max_sweep_per_cycle: 64
  hard.enabled: true
  hard.cooldown_ms: 10000   # min time between hard compactions
  pressure.threshold_ratio: 0.82 # trigger hard when resident/limit > 0.82
  backoff.multiplier: 1.5
  safety.max_cpu_pct: 0.15 # never spend more than 15% cpu on compaction work
```

jonathan: sounds reasonable. my only worry is long-term fragmentation: if we delay hard compaction too much we may OOM-increase and then be forced to do massive work. need an escape hatch.

lee: escape hatch = maintenance window compaction + admission pressure. algorithm: keep a rolling estimate of fragmentation_ratio = free_frag_bytes / total_free_bytes. if fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 and resident > threshold -> escalate immediately. also schedule a staggered compaction across nodes to avoid cluster-wide spike. pseudo: 

```
if fragmentation_ratio > FRAG_HIGH and resident_ratio > PRESSURE:
  mark_tenant_for_hard_compact(tenant_id)
  schedule_hard_compact_with_jitter(tenant_id, jitter_ms)
else if time_since_last_hard < cooldown:
  perform_soft_compact()
else:
  maybe_no_op()
```

maria: also need to coordinate with prefix/KV cache eviction. if prefix hits drop, we should avoid compacting the same ranges. add a short-lived compaction-block token when eviction is active.

infra-bot: deploy-check: compaction-safeguards branch CI passed: https://ci.redwood.example/compaction-safeguards/42 (reaction :white_check_mark:)

jonathan: for safety, add an emergency-throttle metric that flips to pause all compaction if we detect >5% increase in tail latencies within 1m of compaction start. better to slow growth than fix it post-factum.

rachel: will add metrics and a dashboard mock in next PR. suggest an "incidents" alert when compaction_paused_reason == "tail-latency-protect" so SRE/regression teams can triage.

devx: doc note: mention that Dedicated customers can set `safety.max_cpu_pct` per pool. also add a short section in runtime-ops about rolling compaction and how to interpret the new metrics.

maria: action items: 1) lee to draft scheduler impl + unit tests, 2) rachel to add metrics + dashboard, 3) devx to update config docs and gating for Dedicated, 4) i'll add the compaction-block token and emergency-throttle. want a lightweight eng-runtime RFC nudge once PRs are up. thanks everyone. :shipit:
